title: EIP-8449: Engine API Proposal Lookahead
description: The consensus layer tells the execution layer, ahead of time, at which slots it will ask for a payload
author: Csaba Kiraly (@cskiraly)
bodyPreview: ## Abstract This EIP adds an Engine API method, `engine_proposalLookaheadUpdatedV1`, with which a consensus layer client (CL) tells its execution layer client (EL) the slots, timestamps, fee recipients and target gas limits of the blocks its validators are scheduled to propose in the current and next epoch. It is a notice, not a command: it starts no build, names no parent block and changes no consensus rule. The EL uses it to prepare for those blocks in ways that do not need the parent block: fetching blob data, warming the state, pre-executing pending transactions, and keeping its own heavy work and network traffic away from the slot. ## Motivation ### What the EL knows, and when In the Engine API up to and including Amsterdam, an EL learns that it has to produce a block when the CL calls `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` with payload attributes, which also starts the build. The call names the head to build on, and the attributes depend on it: the parent beacon block root, and `prevRandao` and the withdrawals, computed from the parent's state advanced to the proposal slot. A CL can send attributes before the parent arrives, but they then start a build on its current head, which will not be the parent. In practice, the notice starts when the parent is imported. When CLs send it varies. Before Gloas, Prysm, Teku and Grandine send it on the parent's import, Lighthouse and Lodestar 4 seconds before the slot, and Nimbus 1.5 seconds before; only Lighthouse's lead can be configured. Even the earliest leaves only what remains after the parent arrives: at least 8 seconds when the parent is on time, by 4 seconds into its slot, and more only when the slot before it was empty. The CL knows much earlier. Since [EIP-7917](./eip-7917.md) the proposer lookahead for the current and next epoch is part of the beacon state, so every proposal is known at least one epoch, 6.4 minutes, before its slot. Of the payload attributes, the timestamp, the fee recipient and the target gas limit are known as early. In the consensus specifications for Gloas, the consensus side of the fork that brings [EIP-7732](./eip-7732.md), a CL already [lists these slots](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/460fd37c3a58f6baf8a9a285d2adf71c4f818929/specs/gloas/validator.md#broadcasting-signedproposerpreferences) for its validators and may broadcast its preferences for them, the fee recipient and the target gas limit, to builders. Its own EL is not told. ### Preparation that does not need the parent A large part of what an EL can do to produce a block well does not depend on the parent block. Only the EL knows how much time it needs for this preparation, so trying to drive it with the timing of `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` is not ideal. Some examples, without trying to be exhaustive: - **Blob data.** With the sparse blobpool ([EIP-8070](./eip-8070.md)), an EL fetches the full blobs of only some blob transactions and samples the rest, but to include a blob transaction it needs its full blobs. EIP-8070 therefore has local builders fetch the full blobs of every blob transaction they may include, all the time, at about four times a sampling node's blob bandwidth. It mentions the option of switching to that mode 2 to 3 slots before building, and advises against it because the switch is a visible pattern that compromises the builder's privacy and raises its risk of denial of service. Without notice an EL cannot make the switch at all; with notice minutes ahead it can make it at a randomized time, which gives limited protection where the node has no other. - **State.** Executing the chain keeps warm the state that recent blocks touched, but not the state that pending transactions will touch. That can be read into the EL's caches before the slot, so that the build does not wait on the disk for it. - **Pre-execution.** Pending transactions can be executed ahead of time with the announced timestamp, fee recipient and gas limit, and the results carried from head to head. A result can be reused only while everything it depended on still holds: the state it read, the block context it used, and what the transactions before it in the block changed. - **The EL's own heavy work.** Database compaction, flushing state to disk, history pruning and similar maintenance can be kept away from the proposal slot. - **Bandwidth.** Around its slot, the EL can hold back its own transaction and blob gossip, as far as its role in the network allows, so that the CL's block and data columns ([EIP-7594](./eip-7594.md)) get the node's uplink. Like the switch to full blobs, this is visible to peers and needs the same care. A node that builds every slot, as a professional builder does, can do all of this all the time. A validator proposes rarely. Without notice, whatever it prepares is mostly for blocks it will not build: it can prepare continuously and pay for it, prepare within a small budget and gain little, or not prepare at all. ### Shrinking timelines Several changes shorten the time between knowing the parent and the slot, or add work to it: - With enshrined proposer-builder separation (EIP-7732), an execution payload is revealed after the beacon block that commits to it, by the middle of the slot. A proposer that builds on that payload can form its payload attributes only once the payload is imported. By the deadlines, the time between a parent on time and the next slot shrinks from 8 seconds (a beacon block is on time until 4 seconds into its slot) to 6 (a payload is on time until 6 seconds into its slot), before the time it takes to import it. Building on the parent without its payload is possible sooner, but fork choice selects that only when the payload is late or missing. The proposer's own payload must still be complete at the start of its slot, because its beacon block commits to the payload's hash. - The gas limit was raised to 60M ([EIP-7935](./eip-7935.md)), and core developers have agreed on 200M for Glamsterdam, the fork that brings EIP-7732 and
